# Ordinary public FIPS state owner

This bounded contribution supplies public crypto.getFips(), crypto.setFips(value), and the nonenumerable, nonconfigurable deprecated crypto.fips accessor for the ordinary, non-forced process mode admitted by the current CLI. It uses the actual linked ncrypto/OpenSSL default-property state; it does not report provider installation, algorithm availability or certification. No public SubtleCrypto/normalizer activation is included.

The existing263 internal state/generation getter,262 WebIDL isFips cache and264 MAC-generation inventory are retained. The new native setter shares their real state mutex, calls ncrypto::setFipsEnabled with primitive truthiness, and relies on ncrypto's actual atomic generation change only after a successful mode transition. Repeated equal values do not increment generation. Genuine main-versus-Worker authority comes from ShellContext::isWorker; the public Worker path throws the pinned ERR_WORKER_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION before argument coercion, and raw internal mutation retains the target's fatal process-state admission. There is no JavaScript fd/tag/state flag or host production delegate.

The JS public ordinary branches and deprecated descriptor follow pinned Node26.13.0 lib/crypto.js265–280/357–365. ToBoolean does not invoke valueOf or Symbol.toPrimitive. Method receivers and extra arguments are ignored. Deprecation uses the existing real utility/warning owner and exact DEP0093 text, with separate getter/setter wrappers. The native CryptoErrorList owns real queue strings, chooses its last message and prior opensslErrorStack strings without numeric error decorations, and preserves the exact lowercase empty-list "ok" fallback from env_properties.h. Actual transition and complete error-string capture/copy are serialized; error JS creation/property publication happens after unlock so an inherited setter cannot reenter this owner's held mutex. The exact Node native implementation retains its native locks through its ordinary property Set; no Node defect or executed failure-path parity is asserted here.

Forced startup remains missing. The current CLI rejects --enable-fips/--force-fips; this slice does not invent a false forced-state flag or pretend those modes were admitted. Exact target --force-fips provider/strict policy, OpenSSL configuration initialization, provider/self-test admission, immutable force state, forced-mode public wrapper branch, indicator events and Worker startup propagation need a separate owning slice. Any future admission must connect both public forced behavior and the native forced-mutation CHECK before activating it. Non-FIPS provider/configuration failures and certification cannot be replaced with manufactured availability errors. OpenSSL3 may enable its default FIPS property without installing a FIPS provider, as the pinned target does; this does not make later crypto operations succeed.

Evidence is explicitly native dependent: seven native public groups and seven actual candidate-JS-over-V8-private-binding groups match exactly, including truthiness/generation, descriptor shape, ignored receivers, captured functions and real Worker mutation errors. The original fixture's failed primordial import remains recorded. No candidate C++, JSAPI, guest OpenSSL artifact, guest entropy, error-failure publication, raw-worker fatal entry, concurrent crypto/default-property mutation or four-host execution was performed. Native mode restoration ran in finally. The actual host is Darwin arm64 with the pinned Node26.13.0 binary; its OpenSSL configuration is not the guest artifact/configuration receipt. There were zero compilation attempts and no normal generation or package/overall suite.

Audit relationship: crypto-contracts.md's Metadata/FIPS/secure heap/engines row139 is directly partial for these ordinary APIs; crypto-requirements.json memberRequirements['node:crypto'].getFips/setFips/fips is exact API scope. C-015 is a related broad/prose group, not a new invented numbered FIPS finding. Existing audit definitions and all other crypto gaps remain unchanged.

Integration requires additive shared bootstrap/build.py/curated-adapter hunks over the actual later source, exact native-digests.cpp leaf admission, two normal shell registrations, and declaration of crypto-fips-platform-adapter.js as a new recipe input. Parent regenerates current core once with its next coherent batch. No generated core, recipe revision, patch number, ABI change or old whole shared-source replacement is supplied here.
